dedupe_keys.name: port operations lab and miniportsim container terminal simulator

description: Port Operations Lab is a Python workspace for building a container terminal digital twin and optimisation stack, published on GitHub in 2026 by the developer Yasin Ege Akıcı. Two of eight planned projects are complete: a terminal operations core with domain entities for vessels, berths, quay cranes, yard blocks and container groups, immutable events and state snapshots, atomic commands and an interactive Streamlit control centre; and MiniPortSim, a scenario-driven discrete-event simulator with vessel arrivals, berth allocation, crane and yard constraints, stochastic disruptions, metrics, replay files and experiment runners. Planned projects cover berth allocation baselines, quay crane scheduling, yard relocation, a reinforcement learning environment, AIS-based calibration of port calls and a benchmark engine. Coverage: a generic, synthetic terminal defined by scenarios. Access: source code and tests on GitHub. Licence and cost: MIT licence, free. Caveats: an early personal project without peer review, validation against a real terminal or AIS calibration yet, so results are illustrative; it suits teaching and benchmarking more than planning decisions. It supports capacity planning and optimisation experiments for port operations and disruption response. It complements the SmartPort inland logistics digital twin case study in the catalogue.
